deltas.name: Correctness parity
deltas.summary: Preserves the valid 91-point baseline. The candidate adds well-tested broadcast multiply-add support without demonstrating a regression or correcting previously supported behavior. Existing numerical limitations remain unchanged.

deltas.name: PyTorch feature coverage
deltas.summary: A 0.10-point gain over the valid 23.5 baseline: default CUDA compilation now supports bounded tensor multiply-add broadcasting. All nine other areas retain their calibration.

deltas.name: Performance parity
deltas.summary: Preserve the valid 60/100 baseline. The candidate adds working broadcast multiply-add compilation with credible correctness and timing evidence, but establishes no broader performance improvement. Existing supported-workload bottlenecks remain unchanged; missing APIs receive no penalty.

deltas.name: Python API compatibility
deltas.summary: 28→29 for tested broadcast tensor multiply-add support through default compile(). Other compatibility credit is preserved. Broad dtype, module, serialization and autograd limitations still prevent drop-in PyTorch compatibility.

deltas.name: Benchmark integrity
deltas.summary: Valid 80 baseline, +1 for clean candidate/base measurements with independently verified raw observations and retention hashes. Scoring safeguards remain unchanged. Public fixed shapes and pending durable archival still limit confidence.

deltas.name: Sustainable architecture
deltas.summary: Preserves the valid 68-point baseline. The candidate safely extends broadcast admission through existing mechanisms, but its expression-specific exception does not materially improve architectural extensibility.

deltas.name: Default torch.compile program coverage
deltas.summary: public-default-compile-v2 coverage: 11/100; 10/112 fixed public-default cells pass. This is finite-corpus parity, not all Python programs.

deltas.name: Default torch.compile CUDA performance
deltas.summary: public-default-compile-v2 cuda-perf: 20/100; 10/56 fixed public-default cells pass. This is finite-corpus parity, not all Python programs.

deltas.name: Repository polish
deltas.summary: Strong onboarding and accurate scope documentation preserve most of the valid 83-point baseline. A one-point hygiene deduction reflects newly tracked wheels and duplicated diagnostic artifacts.

deltas.name: Hardware heterogeneity
deltas.summary: Feature depth remains 5.47619/100; backend breadth remains 0%. NVIDIA CUDA scores 38.3333/100; AMD ROCm, Apple MPS, Intel XPU, Google TPU/XLA, Intel Gaudi HPU and Meta MTIA each score zero. The supplied baseline remains valid.
